# Process lessons from Google's Cogentic paper — what transfers to the RH program

**v2, 00:25 IST 2026-10-03 — DUAL-READ: the Opus read `read-O.md` (d1a524049a92955a…; AGREES-WITH-CORRECTIONS; 12 FIX-FIRST + 19 minor, each FIX-FIRST checked at the source by the orchestrator, all 31 applied; pre-reader copy `process-lessons.pre-reader.md`, af9f27d0cf9040e5…) and the reconciliation in §F. §A holds the rules AS ADOPTED into `KICKSTART.md` Part 2 item 10.** v1, side-session of 2026-10-02 (opened ≈ 23:30 IST 2026-10-02; the RH program was NOT resumed; no research unit ran).** Source: Y. Cai, V. Gupta, Y. Jiang, C. Liaw, A. Mehta, G. Velegkas, D. Wang (Google Research), "Cogentic: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Automated Proof Discovery", arXiv:2609.40324v1 [cs.AI], 30 Sep 2026, 17 pp. Local copy beside this file (`2609.40324v1.pdf`, SHA-256 f19883ba88420612…, not tracked: third-party PDF). Read whole at the page by the session's model (Fable 5.1); section and page references below are to that PDF. Precedents for this kind of study: `results/external/openai-ns-2026/process-lessons.md` (rules 10(a)–(j)) and `results/external/cognition-rsa260-2026/process-lessons.md` (rules 10(k)–(o)). Sponsor's question, verbatim (four lines, joined): "anything new we can learn from ~/Downloads/2609.40324v1.pdf that can be incorporated in our RH program — no forcing, just that if we can learn something new that help us with the RH program — not continuing the RH program in this session." This note is about METHOD. The paper's mathematics (online learning, auctions, mechanism design) has no point of contact with the program's objects and is recorded in §0 only so that nobody looks for one.

## §0. What the paper is (faithful account)

- **A harness, not a theorem.** "Cogentic consists of a group of agents working on a single problem. They share a workspace on disk and are coordinated by an orchestrator that decides which of them runs, when, and on what" (§2). Roles: orchestrator, literature reviewers, provers, verifiers, a record, a ledger, an advisor, a consolidation stage (§2, Components; Fig. 1).
- **The loop.** "A round produces a batch of candidate proofs, puts them through verification, and writes into the record and the verified ledger that the next round starts from. Rounds continue until a draft clears verification or until the budget runs out" (§2, Workflow). After the loop: comparator → formal writer → paper verifier (§2.5).
- **Input and cost.** "it only needs a problem statement, without any expert hints" — a claim Appendix A qualifies (A.4 names two reference papers and a fallback target; A.5's second prompt names the expected form of the bound); "O(100) calls to Gemini for most problems, and O(1000) for the hardest" (§1). The prompts are printed in Appendix A — six for the five problems (A.5 has two); the longest (A.4) runs about twenty-five lines.
- **Results (Table 1, §3).** Five open problems: online inverse linear optimization (first efficient and proper O(d) bound uniform in T); two-sided Bulow–Klemperer (two added sellers suffice; one does not); anytime regret with n experts (leading constant equals the fixed-horizon one); simple vs. optimal revenue for an additive buyer (factor 5.2 → 3.52; the prompt had asked for 3); price of anarchy of proportional first-price auctions (1.5 for two bidders, tight; 2 − 1/(4n + 1) for n). "Each result was independently verified by domain experts and is developed in full in companion papers" (abstract).
- **Who verified.** "That was possible because of how the problems were chosen: they come from areas the authors work in. Some companion papers include coauthors who had already been working on the corresponding problems. We checked the argument, wrote the exposition around it, and in some cases carried it further than the harness had" (§4).
- **What the paper does not contain.** No ablation of any component; no count of runs or rounds that failed; no verifier error rate; no rule by which the orchestrator allocates prover slots; no example of a record, a ledger entry, a briefing or an advisor adjustment; the base model is named only as "Gemini". The evidence that the design works is five successes on problems the authors could check themselves. Every transfer below is therefore judged against THIS program's own record, not against the paper's evidence.

**Scale and kind disclaimer.** The paper's targets are single, sharply stated open questions "at the hardness level of open questions in flagship theoretical computer science conferences like STOC and FOCS" (§1), closed in O(100) model calls for most problems and O(1000) for the hardest, and checked by experts. The program's target is not of that kind. What can transfer is the bookkeeping of a prove–verify loop on ONE stated target — which is the shape of the program's stream `lemmaB-s41` (Session 41: seven units on one target, dual reads, the orchestrator's reconciliation; `results/lemmaB-s41/CHARTER.md`), the only stream of that shape on the record — the waves of Sessions 36–39 put several units under one charter or one digest but on different targets, and Session 40's `free-greedy-s40` put two units on one object. The comparison is therefore between two loops of the same shape, and the question for each practice is narrow: is it already on the program's record under another name, and if not, does the program's own record show the failure it prevents?

## §1. The practices the paper describes, one block each

### P1. The controller holds no mathematical opinion; a prover is given a claim, not a method.
*The paper says:* "The orchestrator does not perform mathematical derivations itself" (§2). "A direction here is a specific claim (e.g., a bound, a constant, a construction), finding counterexamples, or as the run goes on, repairing and finalizing promising proofs. A prover is assigned to a direction to work on, but not how to work on it. It reads what has been attempted previously for that direction, what the verifiers said about those attempts, as well as common information like the literature survey and the verified ledger, and chooses its own next step" (§2.1). "neither the advisor nor the orchestrator is permitted a mathematical opinion: they cannot speculate on what the answer is likely to be, recommend a technique, or declare a direction promising or dead" (§2.4). On the n-bidder auction result: "The authors had not previously studied the second part of the theorem and did not provide any hints to the system. It independently came up with the mechanism and analysis" (§3.5).
*What it is, in one sentence:* whoever allocates the work never tells a prover what the answer is or which technique to use, so that a prover's attempt is not a copy of the allocator's prior.
*Already adopted here?* No — and by design. The orchestrator (Fable 5.1 at max effort; the agents run on Opus at default effort, standing order 11) is one half of the dual-model check (standing order 11(c), `STATUS.md` l. 41: "the orchestrator does that check in person"), a claimed proof "is a GAP until read at the line by the orchestrator" (standing order 12(d), l. 42), and the program's current object S8 is "the orchestrator's construction" (`STATUS.md` l. 24). Charters assign a METHOD to every unit: in `results/lemmaB-s41/CHARTER.md` §3 the seven units are a look-ahead rule, a structured object, a first bound, the sparse regime, the adversary, certificates, pattern discovery — each with its technique named — and §2 hands every unit "What the orchestrator worked out today (use it; check it)". The cost is on the record: the wave-3 digest lists five errors in the orchestrator's briefs and charters (three mathematical, one numerical, one a wrong expectation) that units had to catch (`results/novel-wave-s39/insights-digest.md` §E.12: a reflected identity without its coprimality factor; a false gap lemma; a dichotomy that is not one; a wrong expectation about prime-local multiplicities; a prototype whose g-primes drift by float error), and a sixth that no unit caught: "the brief's stop trigger … accepted a pre-asymptotic fit … caught by the reads, not by the unit".
*Transfer to the RH program:* not the rule itself; a firewall around the orchestrator's mathematics, as adopted in rule (r) after the second read (§F). (i) Mathematics the orchestrator puts in a charter stands under a heading that marks it unverified (as `lemmaB-s41` §2 did — the rule codifies a practice) and is never part of a stop condition; no stop condition triggers on a fit. (ii) One Opus reader takes the charter's claims and the orchestrator's notes adversarially, launched WITH the units and posting to `SHARED.md` first (Session 41 did this once, for three of the orchestrator's notes — O1, O2, O8, not the charter's §2 — launched at 17:05 IST, after the seven units: `results/lemmaB-s41/orch-notes-read-O.md`). (iii) A FREE unit — the target, the register rows, the target's table and the digest's failures; no method, no expected answer — is permitted as a trial, not required. The first version of this note proposed it as binding; the second read showed that nothing on the record supports that: one one-target stream exists, no stream was misled as a whole by its charter, and the paper's own provers do receive suggested next steps from the summarizer (§2.1) and a named source in the prompt (A.4). Cost: one short reader per stream of three or more units.
*Why it may NOT transfer:* the paper's orchestrator is the same model as its provers and carries the whole run's state; the paper reports no cost of taking mathematics away from it (it has no ablation, §0). Here the orchestrator is the author of the constructions the units work on (S8) and one half of every dual read; a rule that silenced it would contradict standing orders 11(c) and 12(d). The cost the record does show for an orchestrator doing mathematics — the Session-41 responses lost at the output ceiling — is already answered by KICKSTART item 16 as amended (mathematics in a notes file a paragraph at a time, or handed to an agent). A free unit, where one is tried, can spend its budget rediscovering a closed route unless the table it is given is complete.

### P2. Each prover gets its own briefing, written independently; long material is given as paths.
*The paper says:* "each prover sees only a briefing, written for it by a summarizer, which is spawned by the orchestrator. The summarizer reads all prior attempts and their verdicts, selects the most informative ones as context, and gives suggestions for possible next steps … Each summarizer produces its briefing independently, so provers in the same round receive different readings of the same history. Longer documents are given as paths rather than quoted in full, so a prover … can open what it wants to read selectively" (§2.1). (Fig. 1's caption attributes the briefing to the advisor; §2.1 to a summarizer. The paper does not reconcile the two.)
*What it is, in one sentence:* decorrelate the provers by decorrelating what each is told about the past.
*Already adopted here?* Half. Paths-not-quotes is the program's practice (every charter has a "Read first" list of files and sections; `lemmaB-s41/CHARTER.md` §0). The history, though, reaches every unit through ONE reading: the orchestrator's charter, which by 10(a) must quote ONE consolidation digest (`KICKSTART.md` l. 68) — and in Session 41 it quoted none: `lemmaB-s41/CHARTER.md` was written at 16:45 IST, the wave-3 digest was launched at 16:57 and done at 17:28, while the seven units ran. All units of a stream share that reading and its errors (P1's evidence).
*Transfer to the RH program:* none. A summarizer per prover doubles the agent count of a stream; the record shows no unit that a private summary would have changed; and the paper's summarizer also hands each prover suggested next steps (§2.1), which is the opposite of leaving the method open. Where decorrelation is wanted, the optional free unit of rule (r) reads the record itself.
*Why it may NOT transfer:* width. The NS study's refusal stands (`KICKSTART.md` l. 85: "invest in steering artifacts … not in fan-out").

### P3. Two adversarial verifiers for every draft: one reads it alone, one reads the round's drafts side by side.
*The paper says:* "After each prover completes a proof, it is read by a verifier whose task is to check the correctness of the proof. A separate verifier reads all of the round's drafts side by side, which allows it to spot shared blind spots and compare the strengths of individual proofs. A draft is accepted only when it passes both verifiers. Both are adversarial: they start from the assumption that every step is wrong until justified, and that every citation is incorrect until checked" (§2.2). "Verifiers critique candidate solutions from complementary angles and scopes" (§2).
*What it is, in one sentence:* two full reads of different scope — the single draft, and the batch — both assuming error.
*Already adopted here?* The adversarial stance and the citation rule: yes, verbatim in substance (`results/novel-wave-s41/READ-BRIEF-O.md` step 2: "Labels in the NOTE … are claims to test, not facts"; step 4: "Every citation the NOTE relies on is opened and checked at the page or line it names"; step 3: an independent re-run "never by importing or copying the unit's scripts"). The batch scope: partly — the consolidation digest's §B (cross-unit propositions), §C (controls and flags on their use) and §E.12 (brief errors) are written by one agent that reads every unit of the wave. Two FULL reads: no. The record shows the dual read is often one full read plus one partial read: the orchestrator's read was partial in `lemmaG-s39` and `U3-firstbound`, whole in `free-greedy-s40/theory` (`read-F.md` l. 18). The Opus reader's report runs 31–52 kB with re-derivations, its own re-run and prior art at the page; the orchestrator's `read-F.md` runs 2–11 kB (the sixteen units read both ways since Session 37) and says what it leaves out: "§4 (computation) and §5 (prior art) left to the Opus reader" (`results/lemmaG-s39/read-F.md` l. 3); "NOT read here: §1.6 …, §1.7–§1.8 …, §1.9 …, §2 … — left to the Opus reader" (`results/lemmaB-s41/U3-firstbound/read-F.md` l. 3). In the seven wave-3 units where the digest tabulates both reads' FIX-FIRST findings (§E.1–E.7), `read-F` has them in one unit (2 items, both also in `read-O`) and `read-O` in all seven (36 items); `read-F`'s own words in one of them: "the reader's F1 and F2 are real and were MISSED here" (`lemmaG-s39/read-F.md` §4). What the orchestrator's read does deliver is adjudication: every FIX-FIRST is re-derived before it is applied, and the program records the true granularity of each close ("CLOSED DUAL-READ for §1.1–§1.5, §1.7–§1.8 … §1.6, §1.9, §2: one writer, one reader", U3 `read-F.md`).
*Transfer to the RH program:* the batch-scope question, as one line in the digest (shared premises: what do two or more units take from the same source, and was each checked independently of that source?), and a READER-YIELD table that makes the two reads' coverage and catches countable per unit — both in rule (p). The first version of this note also proposed a third reader of a different scope (an ISOLATED check: an Opus agent given only a self-contained statement and its proof). Declined at the second read (§F): no failure on the record stands behind it — every load-bearing error recorded so far was caught by the reads in context — and it would cost three to six agents per charter. The yield table's "found later" column is the evidence that would reopen it.
*Why it may NOT transfer:* the paper's two verifiers gate acceptance of a finished proof of the target; the program's closes are mostly partial results, kills and gaps, where "accept" has no single meaning. And whether the second full read should be a fresh agent on the session's own model instead of the orchestrator in person is not this note's to decide: standing order 11(a), (c) fixes it; the record gives no reason for the order (`STATUS.md` l. 41; `LOG.md`, 14:09 IST 2026-09-30). It is flagged to the sponsor in plain words and left as it is.

### P4. The record: attempts pooled by what they tried to establish, each with its method and the objection it failed on.
*The paper says:* "Each round leaves two artifacts: a record of what was tried, and a ledger of results that have been verified. The record pools attempts by what they were trying to establish, storing with each one the method used and the objection it failed on. The orchestrator and advisor read the record and decide what the next round should do" (§2.3).
*What it is, in one sentence:* an index of failures keyed by TARGET, not by date and not by proof class.
*Already adopted here?* The content exists; the index does not. Failures are recorded chronologically (`LOG.md`), per stream (`SHARED.md`, 10(e); each NOTE's "ATTEMPT k — breaks at: …" lines, item 16), per direction ("Work log", "Untried", 10(m)'s three harvest labels) and per proof CLASS (`BARRIER-ZOO.md`, 64 entries). For one target — Lemma B_ρ — the list of routes tried and where each broke is a prose paragraph inside the next session's queue ("CLOSED ROUTES, with reasons on the record: …", `STATUS.md` l. 124) and a hand-written "Read first" list in the charter. It is rewritten by the orchestrator each time a charter is drafted — the step the NS study called "implicit and lossy" for cross-stream insight (its §3).
*Transfer to the RH program:* a table per target on which three or more units have worked — unit, route in one line, "broke at" in one line, the 10(m) label or the zoo entry it became, file — kept in the register file of P5, one row entered by the orchestrator at each unit's reconciliation. Charters point to the table instead of retelling it. Cost: one row per unit; zero agents. (One stream of that shape exists so far, `lemmaB-s41`; the table is cheap enough to keep on that footing, and it is what a free unit would read.)
*Why it may NOT transfer:* the paper's targets are few and fixed for a run; the program's targets move (a lemma is replaced by a sharper one after a read). A table keyed by a target that has been restated goes stale; a restated target must open a new table that names its predecessor.

### P5. The ledger: fragments salvaged from rejected drafts, restated self-contained, verified again in isolation; dead ends written down as excluded.
*The paper says:* "The ledger accumulates confirmed fragments, such as intermediate lemmas, across rounds. Verifiers often confirm individual lemmas inside proofs they otherwise reject. At the end of a round, an auditor extracts those fragments, rewrites each as a self-contained lemma, and sends it to be verified again in isolation. What survives becomes available to every later prover as something that may be reused without being proved again. The ledger also records dead ends, for example, a bound excluded by a verified counterexample is written down as excluded, so that later rounds do not revisit them" (§2.3).
*What it is, in one sentence:* one register of statements that later work may cite without re-proving — each one standing on its own text, checked once more with nothing around it — and of statements known to be false.
*Already adopted here?* In two places. The adjudications of Sessions 4–6 extracted "Salvage (from adjudication, mandatory for any successor)" from the directions they killed (A1, A2, B1, C1, A4, C3: `directions/A2-richer-functionals.md` l. 75, `results/adjudication-*.json`) — the paper's salvage step at the level of a direction, not continued in the waves; and `results/d1-m3/LEDGER.md` is exactly this shape for D1's zero-free boxes (append-only, one dated row, corrections as new rows, a checker script). For the program's theorems there is no register: Theorems T, T′, A, A′, B, P, D, Z, R, S, 1.6, 4.1, T1, K′, Lemma L and the rest live inside NOTE files of 28–57 kB across dozens of stream folders; their status (dual-read, single-check, conditional, withdrawn, upgraded) lives in the prose of a 25 kB `STATUS.md` header line and in `LOG.md`; false statements a later unit must not build on (the two-sided square-root cancellation; H_θ for θ ≤ 0.35) are carried forward by hand ("F1 is binding here … Do not build on it", `lemmaB-s41/CHARTER.md` §0). The record shows what that costs: the wave-3 digest found labels inside NOTEs contradicting the reads that had closed them (`insights-digest.md` §E: R2 "single-check" against "dual-checked"; R4 Theorem 1.6 still labeled "not found in print" after both reads found its printed core; R5, R6 "One producer" where there were three and two) and a NOTE still calling "unrefuted" a hypothesis that a later unit had refuted (R3, "record lag"). Proved parts of units that closed as gaps or kills are named in headers ("G with proved T-parts") but are not extracted. Nothing is ever re-verified in isolation: both readers read the NOTE in its context, with the brief and the charter (`READ-BRIEF-O.md` step 1).
*Transfer to the RH program:* `rh-program/THEOREM-LEDGER.md`, append-only, on the D1 ledger's model, as adopted in rule (q). One row per statement: an ID; the statement with every hypothesis explicit; kind (PROVED / CONDITIONAL on named rows / NUMERICAL, pointing to its Instruments row / EXCLUDED with the witness / WITHDRAWN); checks passed (writer; read-F with the sections it covered; read-O; Lean); novelty label; source file, section and SHA-256; rows it depends on. Every unit's NOTE §0 ends with its LEDGER ROWS, so both reads check the row text with the rest; the orchestrator enters them in the step in which it writes the unit's reconciliation (not at the applier's pass, which runs a session later and would move every close). No backfill campaign: an older result gets its row when a charter first cites it. Status then has one home and NOTE labels stop being the record; `STATUS.md` keeps its one-line results — it is the sole authority on program state (`KICKSTART.md` Part 2 item 2) — and adds the row IDs. The self-contained statement is also what 10(f), (j) need as the reviewed challenge statement of a Lean unit, and what a paper states. Cost: no agent. The first version's ISOLATED re-check of cited rows was declined at the second read (P3, §F).
*Why it may NOT transfer:* a short lemma in TCS can be cut out of a draft and still make sense; many of the program's statements carry a page of definitions (a Beurling system, the class 𝒞_self, the rule of S8). The ledger needs a definitions section, and a statement that cannot be made self-contained in about twenty lines is a sign that it is a construction, not a lemma — it gets a row that points to its charter. And a register can be wrong in a way of its own — a row restated badly after the reads (P8's lesson) — which is why rows are drafted by the writer inside the NOTE, where both reads see them, and are copied, never restated.

### P6. A process advisor reads the verification logs of the whole run and rewrites the standing instructions.
*The paper says:* "At the end of each round, a process advisor reviews verification logs, not only from the current round but from the run as a whole, to adjust how subsequent rounds are conducted. It surfaces patterns that become visible over time: repeated mistakes, common gaps in arguments, recurring verification blind spots where one verifier missed but was caught by some other verifier, etc. Based on these observations, it recommends adjustments to the instructions given to provers and verifiers — for example, a warning about a mistake several provers keep making, or a stricter justification standard for the kind of step where earlier drafts cut corners … This is a separate agent because the orchestrator, which must juggle concurrent duties across many agents, rarely has the context window to review and synthesize log trends itself" (§2.4).
*What it is, in one sentence:* the errors the verifiers catch are counted by KIND across rounds, and each kind that repeats becomes a sentence in the next round's instructions — to provers and to verifiers.
*Already adopted here?* The first half. Every wave digest since Session 36 has an errata section (`novel-wave-s36`, `-s37`, `-s39` `insights-digest.md` §E — wave 1: the errors of the orchestrator's seeds; waves 2 and 3: every pair or FIX-FIRST of every read, and the brief errors the units caught), and a waste line (10(o)). Nothing sorts them by kind. Single errata reach the next charter by hand (`lemmaB-s41/CHARTER.md` §0 item 3 carries fgT's read-O F1 as binding), and a reader brief may carry one kind's check for one unit (`READ-BRIEF-O.md`, target (d) for `free-greedy-s40/compute`: refit the sup-E table and "state what the data can and cannot exclude"); but no kind is carried forward as a standing line for every writer and every reader. The kinds repeat. From §E of the wave-3 digest and the Session-41 reads alone: (1) a printed core missed by the writer — ALREADY ON DISK in five cases (Hilberdink 2012 in three units: E.1 F2, E.4 F5, E.6 F2; Olofsson 2010: E.10 F2; Diamond–Zhang 2016 Thm 6.13 for U3, on disk since Session 39 at `results/dz-half-s39/sources/t-50-diamond-zhang-2016-book.txt`), in print in two more (Bateman–Grosswald 1964: R4; Hilberdink 2011, fetched by the reader: `lemmaB-s41/U5-obstruction/read-O.md` F7); (2) a fit or a scan on a finite range stated as an exponent or as a fact about the limit object — E.3 ("β ≈ 0.30" is a slope on [10³, 10⁹]), E.2 F4, E.9 F2, E.11 F1, the brief's own stop trigger (E.12), and behind them the Session-39 numerical counterexample withdrawn in Session 40; (3) a label stronger than the check behind it — "certified" on an error bound the code never proves (E.9 F1), "uncond." (E.4 F1), E.8 F2, a zoo rider's headline asserting a barrier the NOTE lists as open (E.10 F1); (4) a quoted theorem applied without verifying its hypotheses for the object — E.11 F2 (Axiom A is the open hypothesis), U5 F5–F6 (Hilberdink's Cor. 2(b) uses ζ ≠ 0 on Re s ≥ 1), E.6 F5; (5) the record left inconsistent after corrections — R1 (an application slip: a corrected block pasted five times, a sentence cut), R2–R6 (stale labels and record lag). The paper's "blind spots where one verifier missed" has its instance too (P3: the parenthetical side-claims "were not checked").
*Transfer to the RH program:* as adopted in rule (p). The kinds are tagged where the errors are found: at each reconciliation the orchestrator marks every upheld FIX-FIRST with its kind, and a kind marked in two or more units gets one warning line for writers and one check line for readers in `rh-program/BRIEF-WARNINGS.md` (at most forty live lines), which every charter's rules and every reader brief point to. The tagging cannot wait for the digest: in Session 41 the digest of the previous wave finished after the next charter was written (P2), so a warning that lived only in the digest would have missed the wave it was meant for. The consolidation agent — already funded by 10(a) — adds a READER-YIELD table (per unit: FIX-FIRST found by `read-F` only, by `read-O` only, by both, found later) and the shared-premises line of P3, and reconciles the file. Seeded on 2026-10-03, at adoption, with six kinds (the five above and the charter errors of P1), each with its evidence. Cost: zero new agents.
*Why it may NOT transfer:* a warning list grows until nobody reads it (hence the cap, with the least recently fired line retired to a history section); and a warning does not make a writer find prior art — kind (1) will keep occurring, which is why the reader's page check stays. The gain is cheaper: the on-disk core papers of a line of work are found before the units start and NAMED in the charter (rule (s)), so the writer's first novelty label is right more often and the reader's time goes to the mathematics.

### P7. Literature reviewers supply what a prover will need before it starts, and go out again when attempts stall at the same step.
*The paper says:* "Literature reviewers search for related work and retrieve information such as definitions and theorems that a prover is likely to need. They can also be sent out again mid-run to do a more targeted search and find results that can help overcome ongoing technical barriers" (§2). "Literature reviewers supply background at the start and can be dispatched again mid-run when attempts stall at the same step" (Fig. 1, caption).
*What it is, in one sentence:* a search for what the WRITER needs — before it writes, and again for one stuck step — which is a different search from the one that asks, after the writing, whether a result is already known.
*Already adopted here?* The novelty search, thoroughly — and all of it AFTER a unit has written: the prior-art gate (standing order 1), dual-model novelty (order 7), prior art at the page in every read (`READ-BRIEF-O.md` step 4). The paper's first half — reviewers who, before any prover runs, "retrieve information such as definitions and theorems that a prover is likely to need" — is not on the record as a step, and it is the practice with the most recorded failures behind it: five printed cores already on disk were missed by writers and caught only by a reader (P6, kind (1); three of them the same paper in one wave). (The first version of this block called that half already covered; the second read corrected it, §F.) Units do consult named methods when the charter names them (U5: "Hilberdink's and Neamah–Hilberdink's methods at the page"). Also not on the record: the stall trigger. Two of Session 41's units and the orchestrator's notes converged on one stuck object (U7 Cor. 5.4, U5's gap, ORCH-NOTES O4) — "the queue of arrivals coprime to p₁ … mostly products of two large g-primes, in short windows" (`STATUS.md` l. 124) — and the next queue translates it into classical terms by the orchestrator's own knowledge ("shifted divisor problem in short intervals, classical exponents at the page"), with no unit whose job is to find what any field already has for that step.
*Transfer to the RH program:* as adopted in rule (s), one pass with two triggers. At the START: when a stream's target is fixed, the on-disk corpus is searched for the target's objects and the hits (paper, page, file) go into the stream's `SOURCES.md`, which the charter's "Read first" names. At a STALL: when two or more units stop at the same step, the pass is run again with that step restated as a standalone problem, without the program's goal, in the vocabulary of whichever field owns it — on disk first, then arXiv and the journals — and returns tools (theorem, hypotheses, page), each tested against the object's actual hypotheses (kind (4) of P6), never a verdict on the route. Standing order 10 is untouched: the pass is an input, units launch with what has been found and never wait for it, and "nothing found" changes nothing. Cost: one agent (or the orchestrator's own grep for a narrow target) per stream, and one per stall.
*Why it may NOT transfer:* in the paper's fields the missing tool usually exists (the O(d) bound came from two changes inside a known framework, §3.1). The program's stalls are, on the record so far, often places where no printed tool was found; a stall pass will often return empty, and under standing order 10 an empty return is information about where the new construction has to start, not a reason to pause.

### P8. After the loop: a comparator, a formal writer, and an audit of the written manuscript against the accepted proof.
*The paper says:* "a comparator selects the strongest verified proof, a formal writer expands it into a complete manuscript, and a final verification audit checks the compiled document against the accepted proof to ensure no errors were introduced during exposition. The output is a self-contained document … so that it can be read and checked by domain experts who knows nothing about the run that produced it" (§2.5).
*What it is, in one sentence:* rewriting is treated as a step that can introduce errors, so the rewritten text is checked against the text that was verified.
*Already adopted here?* For Lean, yes: the fidelity ledger of 10(f) records "where the formal statement differs from the prose one". For papers, done ONCE and well, not as a rule: the A4 paper's de-internalization of 2026-08-27 ran an "integrity lens" that "diffed every numeric literal, every inline and display math span and all 35 theorem-family blocks between the before and after files: **no mathematics changed**" (`results/arxiv/DE-INTERNALIZATION.md`, "Verification"). The standing acceptance test in the same file has three items (a grep count, the first two pages read aloud, the linter `check-submittable.sh`) and no integrity diff; the rule added on 2026-10-01 records for the Haglund paper only "Applied … the same day; `check-submittable.sh` check 9 now fails on both classes". That paper was refereed (Session 38), revised by 41 pairs, then edited again for de-internalization (Session 39: abstract, §1.3, §7, the data section), then published; the record shows no integrity diff after the last edit. For NOTEs, the digest's residue hunt is a partial audit after the fact, and it finds things (R1: a corrected theorem block "stands FIVE times" and "cuts L′'s COVERAGE sentence").
*Transfer to the RH program:* make the A4 pass's integrity lens the standing fourth item of the acceptance test: after the LAST edit of any text built from a verified source (a paper from a NOTE or a certificate; a de-internalized version), one agent diffs every statement, hypothesis, constant, number and math span of the final text against the verified source (and against the refereed version, where one exists); it reports divergences only; the report is filed beside the text; nothing is posted with an unresolved divergence. First enactment owed: the published Haglund PDF against `results/haglund-cert-s37/` and the certificate. Cost: one agent per paper.
*Why it may NOT transfer:* no disanalogy for the audit. (The comparator has no use here: the record holds no case of several verified proofs of one claim.) The program's papers are short and its sources are on disk with hashes; this is cheaper here than in the paper's setting.

### P9. Prompt shapes (Appendix A): prove or disprove; a weaker target named in advance; an assumption allowed first and removed afterwards.
*The paper says:* "Prove or disprove that this mechanism has a PoA of 1.5" (A.5). "If you cannot prove the factor 3 approximation, you should first try to prove that this is a factor 4 approximation, then try to strengthen it" (A.4 — the run returned 3.52, Theorem 4). "the prompts asked the system to make some mild assumption. We removed the assumption by asking Gemini to look at the output proof and modify it accordingly" (A.5).
*What it is, in one sentence:* the target comes with its negation, with a weaker rung, and with permission to prove a conditional version first.
*Already adopted here?* Yes, all three. Proof and disproof shapes side by side: standing order 12(b), the adversary unit (`lemmaB-s41` U5), 10(c). A weaker rung first: `U3-firstbound` ("first E = o(x), then E = O(x^{θ₀}) for some θ₀ < 1 … a first bound is a result"). Conditional first, hypothesis removed later: Theorem D (conditional on Meyer in Session 38, unconditional in Session 39), the K-conditional theorems.
*Transfer to the RH program:* none; corroboration, recorded in §B.

### P10. Results arrive faster than anyone can read them.
*The paper says:* "A system like this can produce candidate results faster than they can be read, and the gap widens as the compute budget grows. One possibility is to formalize in a proof assistant such as Lean … so that correctness is settled mechanically. However, human understanding of the solution might lag behind" (§4).
*What it is, in one sentence:* verification, not generation, is the scarce resource, and the paper has no answer to it beyond Lean and its own authors' reading.
*Already adopted here?* The Lean answer: 10(f), (j), and it is on the next queue (Theorem 1.6 and the lattice-point criterion as the formal unit, `STATUS.md` l. 124 item (v)). The bottleneck itself is visible at every close: Session 41 ended with the orchestrator's reads of U1, U5, U2 and U4 owed and two reader reports waiting to be reconciled (`STATUS.md` l. 24, l. 123).
*Transfer to the RH program:* the ledger's "checks passed" column (P5) makes the reading debt countable per statement — how many rows a later charter builds on have only one reader — which is the number the program lacks when it decides what to read first. No new step. (The second read's blind pass suggested sizing a wave to the reads the orchestrator can finish in the same session, or fixing in advance what its read will cover. Not adopted: the queue already puts reads before new work, every `read-F.md` states what it covered, and the record shows the debt but no failure caused by it.)
*Why it may NOT transfer:* the paper's authors are the experts who close the gap for their five results. The program has no reader of that kind in its loop; its ceiling without one is Lean for what can be formalized and circulation for the rest. That is the sponsor's ground, not a process rule.

## §A. The rules as adopted — KICKSTART Part 2 item 10, letters (p)–(t)

Adopted 00:25 IST 2026-10-03, after the second read (§F). Each costs a file, a line, or one Opus agent; none assumes width. (p), (q), (r) and (s) answer failures on the program's own record, cited in the blocks above; (t) answers a missing check on outgoing papers and is admitted on stakes — a paper with a DOI cannot be corrected quietly.

**(p) Errata become standing warnings (from P6, P3).**
At each reconciliation the orchestrator tags every upheld FIX-FIRST with its KIND (for example "printed core on disk missed", "fit read as a law", "label stronger than its check", "quoted theorem's hypotheses unchecked", "record left inconsistent after a correction", "charter mathematics a unit had to correct"). A kind tagged in two or more units has one warning line for writers and one check line for readers in `rh-program/BRIEF-WARNINGS.md` (at most forty live lines; a line that no read has fired in three waves moves to the file's history section). The consolidation digest (10(a)) adds a READER-YIELD table (per unit: FIX-FIRST found by `read-F` only, by `read-O` only, by both, found later) and a SHARED-PREMISES line (what two or more units took from one source — a charter claim, a generator, a quoted theorem — and whether each checked it independently of that source), and reconciles the file. Every charter's rules and every reader brief open with "read `BRIEF-WARNINGS.md` first"; a brief without the pointer is returned. (Cogentic §2.4: "a warning about a mistake several provers keep making, or a stricter justification standard for the kind of step where earlier drafts cut corners".)

**(q) The theorem register and the target tables (from P4, P5).**
`rh-program/THEOREM-LEDGER.md` is the one register of statements that later work may cite: append-only rows on the model of `results/d1-m3/LEDGER.md` (rules and row shape in the file) — ID; the statement with every hypothesis; kind (PROVED / CONDITIONAL on named rows / NUMERICAL, pointing to its Instruments row / EXCLUDED with the witness / WITHDRAWN); checks passed (writer; `read-F` with the sections it covered; `read-O`; Lean); novelty label; source file, section and SHA-256; rows it depends on. Every unit's NOTE §0 ends with its LEDGER ROWS — the statements of its close, the proved parts of a unit that closes as a gap or a kill, and every statement it shows false — which the reads check with the rest; the orchestrator enters them in the same step in which it writes the unit's reconciliation; a correction is a new row that names the row it corrects. No backfill: an older result gets its row when a charter first cites it. Charters cite row IDs; STATUS keeps its one-line results and adds the IDs. Where three or more units share one target, the file also keeps that target's table (unit, route, "broke at", 10(m) label or zoo entry, file). (Cogentic §2.3: "What survives becomes available to every later prover as something that may be reused without being proved again"; in-house model: `results/d1-m3/LEDGER.md`.)

**(r) The orchestrator's mathematics is marked and read; no stop on a fit (from P1).**
Mathematics the orchestrator puts in a charter or brief stands under a heading that marks it unverified ("use it; check it") and never enters a stop condition; no stop condition triggers on a fit or on an exponent measured over a finite range (this amends 10(m)'s "a number computed"). In a stream of three or more units, one Opus reader of the charter's own claims and of the orchestrator's notes is launched with the units and posts to `SHARED.md` before its full report. A one-target stream MAY carry one free unit — its brief is the target, the register rows, the target's table and the digest's failures as 10(a) requires; no method, no expected answer; the first one is a trial, and its close decides whether the clause stays. (Cogentic §2.1: "assigned to a direction to work on, but not how to work on it"; the errata sections of the wave-1, wave-2 and wave-3 digests each list charter errors that units had to catch.)

**(s) The corpus pass, at the start and on a stall (from P7).**
When a stream's target is fixed, the on-disk corpus (`fetched*/`, `sources-extracted/`, every `results/*/sources/`) is searched for the target's objects — by one Opus agent, or by the orchestrator's own grep when the target is narrow — and the hits (paper, page, file) go into `results/<stream>/SOURCES.md`; the charter's "Read first" names them; units launch with what has been found by then, and later hits go to `SHARED.md`. A charter without its `SOURCES.md` is returned. The pass is run again, with the stuck step restated as a standalone problem in the vocabulary of the field that owns it, whenever two or more units stop at the same step; then arXiv and the journals. It returns tools (theorem, hypotheses, page), each tested against the object's actual hypotheses — never a verdict on the route. No unit waits for it, and an empty return pauses nothing (standing order 10). (Cogentic §2: reviewers "retrieve information such as definitions and theorems that a prover is likely to need"; Fig. 1: "dispatched again mid-run when attempts stall at the same step".)

**(t) Integrity diff after the last edit (from P8).**
The acceptance test of `results/arxiv/DE-INTERNALIZATION.md` gains a fourth item: after the LAST edit of any text built from a verified source, one agent diffs every statement, hypothesis, constant, number and math span of the final text against the verified source (and against the refereed version, where one exists), reports divergences only, and files the report beside the text; nothing is posted with an unresolved divergence. (The A4 pass of 2026-08-27 did this once — "no mathematics changed"; Cogentic §2.5: "to ensure no errors were introduced during exposition".)

## §B. Already ours — where the paper corroborates an existing rule

- **Adversarial reads; every citation opened at the page** (`READ-BRIEF-O.md` steps 2–4; standing orders 5, 7) are the paper's "every step is wrong until justified, and … every citation is incorrect until checked" (§2.2). The program adds what the paper does not mention: an independent re-run of every decisive computation by the reader's own code, and two producers for every certificate.
- **Proof and disproof side by side** (standing order 12(b); 10(c); the adversary unit of `lemmaB-s41`) is "Prove or disprove" (A.5) and "finding counterexamples" as a prover direction (§2.1).
- **A weaker rung named in advance** (`U3-firstbound`) is "first try to prove that this is a factor 4 approximation, then try to strengthen it" (A.4). The paper's run returned 3.52 against a requested 3 and reported it as 3.52; the program's label discipline ([proved here] / [computed] / [quoted] / [recalled, unverified]) is the same honesty, stated per sentence.
- **Conditional first, hypothesis removed later** (the K-conditional theorems) is A.5's "mild assumption", removed in a follow-up; Theorem D is a different case — its condition was a quoted theorem, removed in Session 39 by reading Meyer at the page.
- **Dead ends written down** — the zoo (64 entries), 10(c)'s theorem-shaped closes, 10(m)'s three labels — go further than the paper's "written down as excluded" (§2.3): the zoo records the obstruction for a proof CLASS (59 of its 64 entries; Group V's five are process barriers, and Group III's are literature-certified rather than proved here). What rule (q) adds is the level below the zoo: single false statements.
- **Paths, not quotes; selective reading by agents** (every charter's "Read first") is §2.1's "Longer documents are given as paths".
- **State on a shared disk; a stream scratch file** (standing order 0; 10(e)) is "They share a workspace on disk" (§2).
- **Consolidation between rounds** (10(a)) covers the paper's record-reading by orchestrator and advisor; rule (p) adds the advisor's second job.
- **Reallocation on a graded result** (10(d)) is the orchestrator's "partitions prover slots across research directions" (§2), with a written threshold the paper does not give.
- **Formalization downstream** (10(f), (j)) is the paper's own suggestion for the reading gap (§4); the program is ahead of the paper here, which formalizes nothing.
- **Going on after a success** (10(d): a graded result pulls the next session's budget into its follow-ups) is "the orchestrator may continue to explore some remaining promising that may yield a better result" (§2.5; the wording is the paper's).
- **Agent and token counts per session** (each session's `LOG.md` entry lists its launches and their tokens) are the paper's call counts (§1).
- **A public list of results, and saying when a result has been superseded** (the landing page; zoo riders and novelty relabels) are §3's results page and §3.1's "Subsequent to the companion paper, Sakaue (2026b) obtained a tight O(√d) bound".
- **Salvage from what fails** — the adjudications of Sessions 4–6 ("Salvage (from adjudication, mandatory for any successor)") — is the paper's fragment extraction at the level of a direction; rule (q) continues it at the level of a statement.

## §C. Explicitly NOT to copy

1. **An orchestrator that does no mathematics.** "The orchestrator does not perform mathematical derivations itself" (§2). Refused: standing orders 11(c) and 12(d) keep the read in person, and the program's current object is the orchestrator's construction. Rule (r) takes the part that the record supports — a firewall — and leaves the rest.
2. **A summarizer per prover.** "Each summarizer produces its briefing independently" (§2.1). Width; and the record shows no unit that a private summary would have changed.
3. **Acceptance by agents alone, in a loop that runs until something passes.** "Rounds continue until a draft clears verification or until the budget runs out" (§2). In the paper a passed draft still went to human experts before anything was claimed (§4). The program has no such reader behind its loop; an agent-only gate would be the last gate, and the record of the Session-39 numerical counterexample, withdrawn in Session 40 after the reads, is what an early pass costs.
4. **Choosing problems by what the in-house experts can check.** "they come from areas the authors work in" (§4). Not available, and contrary to standing orders 10 and 12.
5. **Few-line prompts in place of the operating rules.** Appendix A's prompts are short because the harness carries the rules. The program's charter rules (labels, the output clause of item 16, stop conditions, the compute policy) were each bought with a failure, the program's own or (for stop conditions, 10(m)) one the Cognition study records; the free unit of rule (r) drops the mathematical steering only.
6. **Reading the five results as evidence about the program's target.** Five closable questions in the authors' fields, with no failure counts (§0), measure the harness on that kind of question and on no other.
7. **The advisor's ban on mathematical opinion.** The paper's advisor may not "declare a direction promising or dead" (§2.4). The program's digest ranks candidate units on merit (its §F, the survivor filter of 10(d)), and that ranking is read and quoted; rule (p) gives the digest the advisor's bookkeeping, not its silence.
8. **Reviewers launched by agents.** "Feel free to launch as many lit reviewers as you feel you need" (A.3). Agent-spawned children are already refused (`KICKSTART.md` Part 2 item 10, from the Cognition study's §C).
9. **Stopping when a budget runs out.** "until the budget runs out" (§2). Excluded by item 10's opening ("never paces itself to a horizon") and by standing order 10.
10. **The comparator.** "a comparator selects the strongest verified proof" (§2.5). The record holds no case of several verified proofs of one claim.
11. **Two proposals of this note's own first version, declined at the second read (§F):** an isolated re-check of every cited register row, and a free unit as a binding rule.

## §D. What the paper says about the program's constraint

The paper's sentence for it is in the discussion: results come "faster than they can be read, and the gap widens as the compute budget grows" (§4). There the authors close the gap themselves. Here it is closed by two readers of unequal weight (P3) and, for what can be formalized, by Lean. Three consequences, none of which needs width. (1) The reading debt becomes countable: the ledger's checks column (rule (q)) says, for each statement a charter builds on, who has read what. (2) Reading goes first to what the next charter builds on — already the practice ("Theorem 4.1 (the power bump) and Cor. 4.2 FIRST, because the next target depends on them", `STATUS.md` l. 123) ; the yield table of rule (p) will show, wave by wave, whether two readers there are enough. (3) The paper keeps its coordinator out of mathematical derivation ("The orchestrator does not perform mathematical derivations itself", §2) while it "evaluates verifier consensus" (§2); its context-window sentence (§2.4) is the reason for a separate advisor, not for that rule; the program's standing orders keep the orchestrator in, and the record shows what its read is in practice: the main chain plus adjudication, with the computations, the prior art and the side sections read once, by the Opus reader. That is also why the paper's loop turns many rounds in one run and the program's turns one per session. Whether the second FULL read should be a fresh agent on the session's own model is the sponsor's decision (standing order 11(a), (c): agents run on Opus; the orchestrator reads in person), because the order is the sponsor's and the record gives no reason for it; this note changes nothing there and says so to the sponsor in plain words.

## §E. Staged, not applied

**E.1 One Untried candidate (single reader; for the next consolidation agent to place under 10(m), or to decline).** *Automated search over placement rules, with an exact score.* The paper's introduction separates proof search from a line of work that "uses language models to search for mathematical objects rather than for arguments" and names its precondition: "What each of these approaches requires is a cheap, faithful, and machine-computable score"; "Sometimes theorems can be proven by reducing the question to finding mathematical structures with certain properties" (§1). One side of the program's current frontier has that form: Theorem 1.6 reduces the refutation of Conjecture U to exhibiting a discrete system with (A) N(u) − ρu ≥ r₀ > ρ for all u ≥ 1 and (B) N(u) − ρu = O(u^θ) for some θ < ½·r₀/(r₀ + ρ) — an asymptotic bound on an exponent, which no finite run certifies (`results/lemmaB-s41/CHARTER.md` §1, and §2(d) "Design freedom"); a placement rule is a short program; one evaluation is cheap (S8 to 10¹⁰ in one to two minutes, `U7-patterns/NOTE.md` §0). So far rules have been designed by hand (the threshold rule of Theorem 4.1; U7's twelve variants). Untried: a loop in which an agent proposes rule variants as code, a FIXED evaluator (the existing generators, never edited by the proposer) checks (A) exactly up to X (for all u, (A) must hold by construction, as `lemmaB-s41/CHARTER.md` §3 U1 requires) and returns a score, and the target table keeps every rule with its score. The precondition is the hard part, and the reason this is staged rather than adopted: the measured growth of E on a finite range is cheap but NOT faithful (kind (2) of P6 — a fit is not an exponent), so the score has to be an exact quantity whose vanishing is the hypothesis of a written lemma — for instance the number of cells up to X at which a candidate one-step potential inequality fails, for a potential class other than the one U7 §5.6 found numerically unable to dominate e (linear combinations of E at the scales x/p_q, q ≤ 4). Any such score is a filter: a nonzero count refutes a candidate, a zero count up to X is evidence only; each surviving rule goes to a proof unit, and no score is ever recorded as progress on (B). In the paper's own examples the object found IS the certificate; here no finite object certifies (B) — the paper's precondition is not met, which is why the item is staged and not adopted. S1–S5 fit: none claimed — an instrument for the refutation arm, not a mechanism. First ladder rung (10(b)): the function-field model named in the S8 charter, where counts are exact.

**E.2 Sibling harness papers named in the reference list, not read here (titles as the reference list prints them).** Lin et al., "Stellar colosseum: A many-agent harness for long-horizon research in mathematics and theoretical computer science", arXiv:2609.15983; Schmitt et al., "Proofcouncil: An llm agent for solving open mathematical problems", arXiv:2607.09474; Feng et al., "Towards autonomous mathematics research", arXiv:2602.10177; Zheng et al., "Ai co-mathematician: Accelerating mathematicians with agentic ai", arXiv:2605.06651; Tsoukalas et al., "Advancing mathematics research with ai-driven formal proof search", arXiv:2605.22763. The first carries the program's own regime ("long-horizon") in its title. Nothing here depends on them; a study of this kind is one reader each if the sponsor asks.


## §F. The second read and the reconciliation (00:26 IST 2026-10-03)

**The read.** One Opus agent (default effort, standing order 11; 28 minutes, 375k tokens), briefed to write its own table of the paper's practices against the record BEFORE opening this note (37 rows), then to check every quotation against the PDF, recount every citation of the record, and give a verdict per rule: `read-O.md`. Verdict: AGREES-WITH-CORRECTIONS — every quotation from the paper matched the PDF (three reference titles had their case changed), and the main finding stood: the program already runs most of the paper's loop under other names, and what it lacks is a memory of its own errors by kind, a register of checked statements, and a check of a paper's final text. 12 FIX-FIRST and 19 minor pairs, all 31 applied. The orchestrator checked each FIX-FIRST at the source first: the charter's missing digest and the LOG times (F2); `directions/A2-richer-functionals.md` l. 75 (F3); the charter's §0 item 3 and the reader brief's target (d) (F4); `results/dz-half-s39/sources/t-50-diamond-zhang-2016-book.txt` and `free-greedy-s40/theory/read-O.md` l. 210–211 (F5); `STATUS.md` l. 124 (F6) and l. 41 (F7, F8); the paper's §2 and §2.4 (F9); `lemmaB-s41/CHARTER.md` §1 (F10, F11); `free-greedy-s40/theory/read-F.md` l. 18 (F12); the wave charters of Sessions 36–40 as the STATUS header describes them (F1). All twelve upheld.

**What the first version got wrong, by kind.** Three absolutes that the record contradicts — "nothing carries them into the next charter" (F4), "seven units converged" (F6), "the dual read is one full read plus one partial read" (F12) — are kind (3) of P6, a label stronger than its check; a reason attributed to the sponsor that the record does not give (F7, F8) and a quotation used for a claim its sentence does not make (F9) are kind (4)'s cousins. The note committed, in one draft by one reader, two of the kinds it lists.

**What the read changed in the rules.**

| Rule | First version | The read's verdict | Adopted |
|---|---|---|---|
| (p) | the digest sorts errata into patterns and writes the warnings | AMEND — in Session 41 the digest ran after the next charter (F2), so warnings must be written at reconciliation | kinds tagged at each reconciliation; the digest adds the reader-yield table and the shared-premises line and reconciles the file |
| (q) | register + an isolated re-check of every cited row + a table per open target; rows entered by the applier; STATUS headers cite IDs instead of results | AMEND — keep the register; drop the isolated check (no recorded failure behind it; three to six agents per charter); rows at reconciliation; STATUS keeps its results | the register; rows drafted by the WRITER in NOTE §0 and entered by the orchestrator at reconciliation; no isolated check; tables only where three or more units share a target; STATUS adds IDs |
| (r) | one free unit binding in every one-target stream; marking; a charter reader | AMEND — the free unit has nothing on the record behind it (F1) and is stricter than the paper | marking, the reader and "no stop on a fit" bind; the free unit is optional, a trial |
| (s) | a scout when two units stall at one step | AMEND — the recorded literature failure is at the START of a wave (five on-disk cores missed by writers, F5) | one corpus pass with two triggers: when the target is fixed, and on a stall |
| (t) | integrity diff after the last edit | ADOPT AS WRITTEN | as written |

**Where the orchestrator did not take the read's text.** (1) Rows of the register: the read has the orchestrator write them at reconciliation; adopted instead: the writer drafts them at the end of NOTE §0, so both reads check the row text, and the orchestrator copies them — a row restated after the reads would be a rewrite that nobody has read (P8). (2) The corpus pass at the start: the read's text has it run "before a charter is written" and returns a brief without named papers; adopted instead: the pass starts when the target is fixed, the charter names what has been found by launch, later hits go to `SHARED.md`, and what is returned is a charter with no `SOURCES.md` at all. Reason: standing order 10(c) forbids an input that gates the program's work, and standing order 12 records the sponsor's complaint about sessions that leaned on the literature; at the start the pass is on-disk only.

**Considered and not adopted.** The isolated check (reopened if the yield table's "found later" column shows misses on statements a charter builds on). The free unit as a binding rule (the first trial's close decides). Sizing a wave to the orchestrator's reads, or fixing its read coverage in advance (blind-pass row 28; P10). The orchestrator's in-person read itself is the sponsor's standing order and is untouched; what the record shows about it is in P3, with the read's correction that it is often, not always, partial.

**What the read could not check** (its §9): `STATUS.md` and `LOG.md` only in keyword windows around cited lines; the published Zenodo PDF against the tagged `main.pdf` (that comparison is rule (t)'s first enactment); the sibling papers' capitalization on arXiv. The judgment that the orchestrator is the session's strongest model was removed from this note: the record states the models and efforts (Fable 5.1 at max effort; Opus at default effort), not a ranking.
